newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tung's ratings slip, HK newspaper poll shows.
newsitem.headline: Tung's ratings slip, HK newspaper poll shows.

text.p: A poll published on Wednesday by Hong Kong's middle of the road Ming Pao newspaper showed future leader Tung Chee-hwa's ratings slipping from last month.
The survey of 778 residents conducted on Monday rated Tung an average of 4.9 points on a scale from zero to nine for "trustworthiness", down from 5.3 points in a poll carried out on January 30.
He scored 5.2 for "ability", down from 5.4 points, the newspaper said.
Tung was chosen by a Beijing-supervised caucus in December to govern Hong Kong after the British colony's return to China at midnight of June 30 this year.

Between the two polls, Tung accused leading democrat Martin Lee of "bad mouthing" Hong Kong overseas and spreading gloom, after Lee called on the European Union to oppose China's plan to dilute the territory's human rights laws.
